elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Retained 9(b)(ii) says only "the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards" and (vi) that services will be "free from errors that materially affect their utility"; neither is a manner-of-performance warranty ("professional and workmanlike"). No such wording was added.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted (xii): "the Auction Platform and any software or deliverables provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted (xii) sets "a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" — the fallback duration, not 12 months.
9(b)(ii)/(vi) service warranties are stated without any expiry and run throughout the Term (cf. (ix) "now and throughout the Term"), so coverage exceeds 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Inserted remedy sentence: "at Customer's election, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Service, software or deliverable".
Inserted remedy sentence: "or a refund of the fees paid or retained by Kubient for it."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Retained 9(b)(ix): "it is now and throughout the Term shall comply with all applicable Laws in connection with ... the provision of the Service".

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts 9(b) contains a virus/security warranty, but no anti-malicious-code language appears in the rendered operative text supplied (clauses (ii), (vi), (ix)-(xii)); the sub-clause cannot be verified here.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Inserted (xii) expressly warrants that "the Auction Platform and any software or deliverables provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation" "for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" — an express software-to-documentation warranty at the fallback period.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Retained 9(b)(ii) ("the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards") and (vi) (services "free from errors that materially affect their utility") are open-ended warranties operating throughout the Term, comfortably exceeding 30 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Customer's remedy for breach of the warranties in this paragraph 9(b) is, at Customer's election, repair or replacement of the non-conforming Service, software or deliverable" — the remedy is tied to all 9(b) warranties, so it reaches both the services and the new conformance warranty.
"...or a refund of the fees paid or retained by Kubient for it."

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: the single inserted sub-clause (xii) supplies the missing 90-day software/deliverable-to-documentation conformance warranty and the missing repair/replace/refund remedy, and the pre-existing open-ended Service warranties in 9(b)(ii)/(vi) satisfy the ≥30-day services element.

Preferred level fails on duration (90 days rather than 12 months for software) and on the absence of any "professional and workmanlike manner" standard; the no-malicious-code element cannot be confirmed from the rendered text. This is acceptable because the fallback checklist is complete.

Minimal: nothing is deleted, the favourable retained warranties (industry standards, error-free utility, compliance with Laws, Target Bidder reps) and the Section 13 disclaimer carve-out for express warranties are untouched, and the insertion adds no survival tail, expense allocation, procedure or extra damages category. Anchoring the remedy to "the warranties in this paragraph 9(b)" is necessary because the services-warranty remedy element must also be covered.

Two wording choices are customer-favourable variations rather than out-of-checklist requirements and do not defeat minimality: "at Customer's election" instead of the model's "at Vendor's option", and "fees paid or retained by Kubient", which is needed for the refund to have content in a revenue-share structure where Kubient retains rather than is paid a fee. Note them in negotiation as likely trade points.

Preserves intent: Section 13 already excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement", so the new warranty is not swallowed; no cross-reference is left dangling and no retained sentence contradicts the insertion (the numbering follows the existing (ix)-(xi) sequence in 9(b)).
Deviation status is correct: before the edit there was no conformance warranty for any period and no warranty remedy, both material fallback terms.
